title: Midpoint inequality with Euclidean coordinates
statement:
Let $m$ be a natural number, let $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, and let $A,B,C\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $A\ge0$ and $A\le(B+C)/2$. Then
\[
\sqrt{A^2+\sum_{j=1}^m u_j^2}\le\frac{\sqrt{B^2+\sum_{j=1}^m(u_j+v_j)^2}+\sqrt{C^2+\sum_{j=1}^m(u_j-v_j)^2}}{2}.
\]
replaced: Let $m\ge0$, $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, and $A,B,C\in\mathbb R$. If $0\le A\le(B+C)/2$, then $\sqrt{A^2+\sum_j u_j^2}\le\bigl(\sqrt{B^2+\sum_j(u_j+v_j)^2}+\sqrt{C^2+\sum_j(u_j-v_j)^2}\bigr)/2$.
